newsitem.title: UK: Britain bans large calibre pistols from July.
newsitem.headline: Britain bans large calibre pistols from July.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it was banning all large-calibre pistols from July 1 after parliament approved a 150 million pounds ($245 million) package to compensate owners.
Legislation was brought in following widespread horror at the Dunblane massacre last year when a deranged gunman murdered 16 children and their teacher at a Scottish primary school.
Home Office (interior ministry) minister Alun Michael said: "This is an important step towards improving the safety of the public after the terrible events of Dunblane".
Britain now has some of the toughest gun laws in the world, Michael said.
He added: "Around 160,000 large calibre handguns will be taken out of circulation and destroyed."
Parliament will vote on Wednesday on whether to extend the ban to pistols of below .22 inch calibre, which are not covered by existing legislation.
The anti-gun laws have angered target shooters who feel they are being made a scapegoat for the Dunblane massacre and that a legitimate sport will be wiped out in Britain.

Media reports have suggested that target shooters are travelling to France and Belgium to pursue their sport and that ranges are being planned for the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands where the anti-gun laws will not apply.
Owners of large calibre pistols will have to dispose of their weapons by the end of September.
Anyone in possession of a large calibre handgun after October 1 could be sentenced to up to 10 years in prison, the Home Office said.
